# Prototype build: checkpoint

**Every loop iteration: read this file first, do the "Next action", update this file, commit and push.**

**Goal:** a fully functional prototype of everything technical in `docs/DESIGN.md` (v2), without polished UX. Milestones M1–M5; each ends runnable and tested.

## Rules
- Work **headlessly**: no GUI windows. Emulators run with `-no-window`. The user accepts the performance cost.
- **DESIGN.md is the spec.** Where implementation forces a design change, record it here under "Design deviations" and tell the user. Never silently diverge.
- Pending design items (D48, D49, D51, D25, images, "More often") get **pluggable slots**, not full implementations, until decided.
- **Tests:** simulated-network harness for sync logic; property tests for the key-epoch rules; fuzzing for parsers. Heavy network tests only against **local** instances; public relays get at most a few polite test events.
- Dependencies are pinned to exact versions (principle 8). Release profile uses `panic = "unwind"`.
- The Rust workspace lives at the repo root (`crates/`) and excludes `research/`.

## Milestones

### M1: Engine core (Rust)
- [x] Workspace, crates (`kt-engine`, `kt-tasks`, `kt-cli`), pinned deps, CI-style test script
- [x] Crypto primitives: Ed25519 signing, X25519 key wrapping, XChaCha20-Poly1305 with associated data, HKDF derivations, BLAKE3 hashing
- [x] Device identity + PeerID binding (D1); identity store separate from backed-up data
- [x] Personal group and people (display name, list index): `kt-tasks/src/app.rs` (linking semantics in M3)
- [x] Groups and key epochs with the E8 rules 1–8 validated by every receiver (D5)
- [x] Documents (Loro, pinned 1.16.2): group doc + list docs; signed update envelopes; own-ops-only check (D2)
- [x] Import sandbox: validate in a disposable child process; quarantine journal / crash-loop breaker (D3)
- [x] Storage: atomic writes, snapshot + update log, per-group layout
- [x] Soft limits: piece splitting, priority lanes, per-author throttling (D4)
- [x] Document epochs: propose / verify / switch; rebase path; removal cutoffs; concurrent proposals (D24, D26): `kt-tasks/tests/doc_epochs.rs`
- [x] Simulated-network harness + property tests (convergence, removal, impersonation, poison containment): `crates/kt-engine/tests/sim.rs`
- [x] `kt-cli` (`kt`): lists, tasks, share / join bundles, send / recv message files, epochs, info. Two-device demo verified
- [x] Fuzzing of every parser of untrusted input (2026-09-25, `crates/kt-fuzz`: a stable-Rust mutation fuzzer run in ordinary tests; seeds are valid inputs from the real code; encrypted layers are fuzzed from the inside through hidden sealing hooks; failures are saved to `target/fuzz-failures/`). Targets: messages, slot payloads, envelope contents, epoch records, invite records and join requests, whereabouts, LAN beacons, backups (open and restore), typed codes (kt-engine `tests/fuzz.rs`); helper frames and disk copy, P2P frames, DHT refs, Nostr chunks (kt-net unit tests); share links, update and operator manifests, helper announcements, persisted files (kt-net `tests/fuzz.rs`); `.tasklist` files and app restores (kt-tasks `tests/fuzz.rs`). Reach assertions check mutations get past decoding. Long run: 50,000 inputs per target in release, no failures. Long runs: `KT_FUZZ_ITERS=1000000 cargo test --release --test fuzz`

- [x] Capability-based mailbox interface (`kt-net/src/mailbox.rs`)
- [x] Nostr mailbox (`kt-net/src/nostr.rs`): kind 35711, per-device slots, per-relay budget (6/min, burst 5), backoff on `rate-limited:`, 40 KiB chunks with double buffering, read-back health, relay subset per topic
- [x] Sync driver (`kt-net/src/sync.rs`): rewrites only changed / due / lost slots; state persisted across processes
- [x] Local test relay (`kt-net/src/testrelay.rs`, `kt relay`) with rate-limit / size / silent-drop / offline knobs; `kt sync`
- [x] Runs on Android: the `kt` CLI cross-compiled (arm64) on the test tablet syncs with the PC; sandboxed imports work there
- [x] Public relay session (organic, approved 2026-09-24): all edits synced over 7 real relays, kind 35711 accepted everywhere, no rate limits, 100% read-back (`docs/research/E11-public-nostr-session.md`)
- [x] iroh P2P (`kt-net/src/p2p.rs`): whereabouts in sealed slots, slot store, member-to-member exchange with delivery acks, non-members refused, member relaying (store-and-forward)
- [x] Helper relay (`kt-net/src/helper_relay.rs`, `kt helper-relay`): embedded iroh-relay server, token access, per-client cap. **Verified PC ↔ tablet** with Nostr dead: the tablet's sync reached the PC through the helper relay (tunneled over USB with `adb reverse`), 3 slots sent and confirmed, 3 received, 0.62 s on the tablet
- [x] Helper relay TLS without a CA (2026-09-25, `kt-net/src/relay_tls.rs`): self-signed certificate from the endpoint key; one endpoint-wide verifier pins helper relays by IP to their announced key (parsed SPKI, then rustls checks the handshake signature with it) and uses WebPKI roots for named relays. Tests: right pin syncs through a runtime-added TLS relay, wrong pin never gets online (`p2p_sync.rs`); n0 relays still verified (live on the tablet)
- [x] iroh P2P (LAN with rotating IDs, direct, relays per D49 outcome, member relaying): relaying for others done 2026-09-25 (below)
- [x] Discovery via slots (whereabouts) and the **Mainline DHT** (`kt-net/src/dht.rs`, engine `replica/discovery.rs`): sealed, device-signed records at member-only locations that rotate with key epochs. Local testnet test + **public DHT from the tablet**: published and found by the other member device, ~20 s per publish+lookup round
- [x] LAN discovery (`kt-net/src/lan.rs`, D57): beacons with 10-minute rotating tags and sealed device-signed whereabouts, padded entry counts; members learn LAN addresses and dial directly; outsiders learn nothing. Tested on loopback; multicast on a real LAN not yet tested (it would trigger a Windows firewall prompt on this PC)
- [x] P2P membership proof: `Hello` carries the dialer's device-signed whereabouts naming its endpoint, so a responder serves a member it hasn't heard of yet
- [x] n0 DNS discovery as a best-effort layer (`P2pConfig::n0_dns`: pkarr publish + DNS lookup through n0) and n0's public relays added *next to* our own relays (`n0_relays` now keeps the custom map, so helper relays still work); both on in the app (2026-09-25). Before this the app used neither. Live test `kt-net/tests/n0_dns.rs` (`--ignored`) on the tablet: found by endpoint ID alone and fetched in 7.4 s. On the dev PC it can't pass bound to loopback (no home relay without internet on the UDP socket; binding all interfaces would trigger the firewall prompt)
- [x] Android context for iroh (found by the n0 test): iroh's DNS resolver and network monitor call `ndk-context`, which panicked on worker threads because JNA-loaded libraries never get the app Context. Fixed: the app also `System.loadLibrary`s kt_ffi and registers the Context (`kt-ffi/src/android.rs`); `SmokeTest` asserts it on the emulator and the tablet
- [x] Live mode (`kt-net/src/live.rs`): Nostr live subscriptions push members' slots (29 ms locally); knocks (ephemeral kind 25711, throwaway keys, sealed whereabouts) make online members dial each other at once (D49 (b) signaling)
- [x] Helper storage (`kt-net/src/helper.rs`): RAM store for strangers' slots on the device's iroh endpoint (ALPN `kt/helper/1`); signed puts; load-scaled proof of work for new slots (refreshes free); per-topic and young-topic caps; eviction by least recent refresh; session start for restart detection. `HelperMailbox` client (plugs into the mailbox interface) with local reliability records (reachability, latency, withholding, restarts, exclusion). Tested: a stranger's helper carries changes between members who are never online together
- [x] Helper replication (fan-out lists, forwarded signed puts), handoff before going offline, declared evictions
- [x] Self-sustaining Nostr relays (`kt-net/src/relays.rs`, engine `replica/mailboxset.rs`): shipped list is only a seed; discovery from NIP-66 monitors + NIP-65 lists (public data checked: ~240 relays, 21–25 monitors, 3 days); per-group relay set recorded in group data (signed, newest wins); automatic repair when half a set fails; transition writes/reads so no device misses a switch. Test: one seed → discovered set → half the set dies → repaired, still syncing
- [x] Self-sustaining helpers (`kt-net/src/helper_dir.rs`): helpers announce on Nostr under a daily rendezvous; directory; per-group helper set (layer "helpers") created and repaired automatically; untried helpers picked by closeness to a secret daily group point. Test: 4 strangers' helpers discovered, members sync through them only, 2 die, set repaired
- [x] DHT remembers good nodes between sessions (verified on the tablet: 127 → 165 nodes)
- [x] Helper announcements on the DHT (earlier) and **health shared within groups** (2026-09-25): each device publishes its own helper reliability records and relay health as a signed per-member record in its groups' slots (`replica/health.rs`, `kt-net/src/health.rs`); others fold them in at half weight, halving every 3 days; a member's exclusion of a helper (bad data) applies group-wide; only own observations are re-shared (no echo); reports go out with real slot changes and at least daily. Test `health_sharing.rs`
- [x] Member devices as DHT bootstrap entry points (2026-09-25): a device whose DHT node Mainline confirms reachable (not firewalled) shares it in its whereabouts; devices put their members' entry points first in the DHT bootstrap cache, so the DHT layer survives the community bootstrap nodes disappearing. Test `dht_discovery.rs`: B bootstraps through member A alone and finds A's record
- [x] D51 decided (2026-09-24): "Relay connections for others" on by default, desktop only, separate from "Help others sync" (`kt-net/src/settings.rs`; the setting doesn't exist on phones)
- [x] Relaying for others, end to end (`relay_runner.rs`): desktops with the setting on run the TLS relay, announce it only when reachable (public IPv4 on the outbound interface, or an automatic TCP mapping with a public external address), use it themselves; `HelperRef.relay` carries it in announcements; devices keep up to 3 helpers' relays in their relay map (`sync_helper_relays`). Test `relay_for_others.rs`: relay-only phones find a desktop's relay through the normal helper upkeep and sync through it, nothing configured by hand
- [x] Helper reliability: failures don't count while this device is offline (no home relay and no helper answered in 5 min); before, a phone starting offline dropped every helper and their relays
- [x] Helper relays confirmed from outside (2026-09-25): every device probes a helper relay (HTTPS `GET /ping` with the pinned key) before using it and every 10 minutes; a relay that doesn't answer, or answers with the wrong key, is skipped for 6 hours and the next candidate takes its place (up to 3 in use out of 9 candidates). Test: a dead relay and an impostor are skipped. (iroh's own relay measurements need its unstable net-report feature, so not used)
- [x] Helper network: daily-rotated bootstrap point for first joins (2026-09-25): a joiner computes the group's secret daily point from the key its invite carried and adds the helpers closest to it to its join hints, the rule members use for their set (`add_join_hints`); test `join_point.rs`: with no hints, the joiner lands on the members' 8-of-12 helpers. (Also done: helper sets are signed group records in the slots; reliability records shared within groups; phone helping follows Wi-Fi, charging and app-open state)
- [x] Operator manifest (`kt-net/src/manifest.rs`): signed with a separate operator key, add-only merge with the baseline, no downgrade, last good copy persisted; fetch over HTTPS and Nostr (kind 35712, any author, only the signature counts)
- [ ] Operator manifest, real-world part (needs the user): generate the real offline operator key (same handling as the release keystore), choose the hosting URLs (jurisgames.com, the public repo)

### Gaps found against DESIGN (2026-09-25 audit)
- [x] Periodic key rotation (D5 rule 7, `replica/rotation.rs`): due after 30 days, one member in turn (hash-ranked, 6 h cascade), from background sync; additions already make a fresh key; only removals close open invites (refined D7). Test `keys_rotate_periodically_without_closing_invites`
- [x] History (D27): documents record change times; a compaction archives the previous generation with its full history for 30 days (`Replica::doc_archive`); "Undo changes by [person] since [time]" (`kt-tasks/src/history.rs`, `App::undo_changes_by`, list screen "Undo…") puts back tasks added/deleted, fields edited and moves made by that person's devices, leaving others' later edits alone, across compactions. Tests: `history` unit test, `tests/undo.rs` (after a compaction), `DesktopUndoTest`
- [x] **Compaction bug found and fixed**: compacting a group, profile or index document dropped every map except `meta` (a group's list index and names), and equality compared hash-ordered printouts. Rebuild, equality and rebase now cover every root map canonically. Test `compaction_keeps_every_map`
- [x] Text attachments (D4): notes above 100 KB become a blob (LZ4, sealed with its own key, ID = SHA-256 of the ciphertext); the notes field holds marker + reference + a 2,000-character preview, so edits, undo, merges and compaction move them together. Blobs travel by P2P (`kt/blob/1`, served by ID) and through helpers (proof of work, capped, 30-day TTL, re-offered weekly while in use); `.tasklist` files (format 2) and backups (solo lists, up to 16 MB) carry them; unreferenced blobs go after 30 days. Notes dialog in the apps (long notes are read-only until the attachment is here). Corpus v2 records it. Tests `blobs` units, `hold_rules`, `tests/attachments.rs`, `blob_transfer.rs`, `DesktopNotesTest`, `DesktopAttachmentSyncTest`. *Not yet: Blossom as a third layer; members never online together with no helper get the preview only*
- [x] Same-Wi-Fi (LAN) layer in the apps: beacons while open, a direct round when a member is heard, LAN as an invite layer; Android multicast lock while open. Also fixed: `start_live` marked the app closed right after opening it (phone helping never saw the app open)
- [x] Android network changes go to iroh (`network_changed`); phone helping is off in battery saver, below 20 % battery, at severe heat, or with data saver
- [x] Reminders (D43): `remind_ms` on tasks (shared like any field), `set_reminder` / `upcoming_reminders`; Android exact alarms when allowed (inexact otherwise), rescheduled after syncs, on leaving the app, at boot, after updates and when the exact-alarm permission is granted; the permission is asked once when a reminder first needs it (also after a restore); reminder button per task (in 1 hour, tomorrow 9:00, clear); desktop shows due reminders from the tray. Test `ReminderTest`
- [x] Format versioning (principle 8): newer format versions and message kinds decode as `Error::Newer`, not garbage; older devices keep such messages (bounded, 30 days) and pass them on untouched in their slots; "A newer version is available to use certain features" once newer data is seen (Update only via our own manifest); status records v2 carry each device's feature level (v1 still read) and `feature_floor(group)` is the minimum over current members. Test `kt-engine/tests/versioning.rs`
- [ ] Required updates via a manifest signed with the operator key (needs the key; the Play in-app update priority is the other route)
- [x] Golden corpus (principle 8, update policy): `corpus/v1/` is a recorded two-device session: both devices' files, every slot blob they exchanged (epochs, envelopes, statuses, whereabouts, health, names, invites, handovers), a backup and a `.tasklist` file, plus what the lists must contain. `kt-tasks/tests/corpus.rs` opens every generation with the current build (no failed or bad slots, backup restores, file imports, list style reads); `scripts/interop.sh <old-tag>` runs an older release's reader over the newest corpus. New generations only when formats change (`KT_CORPUS_WRITE=vN`), never rewritten
- [x] Keys in OS secure storage (§9): the device identity is kept sealed (`device.sealed`) by the Android Keystore (AES-GCM key, no user auth so background sync works) or Windows DPAPI; an older plain `device.key` is sealed on first load; a failing key store leaves the identity as it was (no lockout); a sealed file never opens without its OS key. Group keys need nothing extra: on disk they are only wrapped for the device key. Tests `kt-engine/tests/vault.rs`, `dpapi_round_trip`, `KeystoreTest`, `DesktopKeyStoreTest`. *Linux desktop: plain file for now (Secret Service not wired)*
- [x] Reserved post-quantum suite ID: wrapped keys carry a suite byte (1 = X25519, 2 = hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 reserved); an unknown suite is `Error::Newer`. Test `unknown_suite_is_newer`
- [x] Splash held until the first sync round (`first_round_done`) or 1.5 s; blocked background sync (Restricted by the user or the OEM, restricted standby bucket, or no periodic run in 2 days while up more than a day) explained once with a button to the app's settings, never requesting the exemption. ## Design deviations
- ~~Epoch records travel unencrypted in M1~~: on the network they now travel only inside sealed slots (M2). The direct join bundle still carries them as-is (M3 invites replace it).
- **Slot event kind 35711, not 31234:** the E4 probe's kind 31234 is registered as NIP-37 "Draft Event". 35711 is unregistered (NIPs README, 2026-09-24). *Needs noting in DESIGN §7.*
- **Previous-generation carry:** after a document epoch each device keeps its own old-generation ops in its slot until every member's signed status shows the new generation (max 30 days). Needed because a device may have edited just before compacting. A device two or more generations behind still can't catch up through slots alone (it needs a member's full export). *Known gap; compactions are rare.*
- **D5 rule 5 made concrete:** removals carry per-document cutoff counters instead of an opaque version-vector digest. Receivers reject a removed device's ops beyond the cutoff; the post-removal document epoch will be rebuilt at the cutoff. *Implementation detail within the design's intent.*
- ~~Own-op send position isn't persisted~~: fixed in M1 (persisted per document, with a durable outgoing queue).
- Groups follow DESIGN §4/§5: a group (a circle of people, the sharing unit) holds one **group document** (`meta.kind=group`, name, `lists` map) plus **any number of list documents**. Solo lists live in the personal group (which also holds the profile and index docs and cannot be shared). Sharing a group shares all its lists, including ones added later. `move_list` copies the live state (task IDs kept) into a new doc in the target group and unlists the old one. Covered by `kt-tasks/tests/app_groups.rs`.
- **Add epochs carry history keys:** earlier epoch keys, wrapped for the new device only, so a new member can read existing content. *Addition the design implied (sharing a list shares its contents); to be noted in DESIGN §5.*

## Tooling notes
- Android builds from Git Bash: `ANDROID_NDK_HOME="$(cygpath -w ~/AppData/Local/Android/Sdk/ndk/29.0.14206865)" cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a -P 26 build --release -p kt-cli`. With `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` (needed for adb device paths) a Unix-style NDK path fails with "os error 3".
- adb: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` for device paths; tunnel PC services with `adb reverse tcp:PORT tcp:PORT` (TCP only).
- Background test relays: run from a *copy* of kt.exe (a running kt.exe blocks rebuilds); Git Bash `timeout` doesn't reliably kill Windows exes.
- `bmgr backupnow` refuses force-stopped apps on Android 15+ ("Backup is not allowed"): launch the app normally first.
- PC network tests bind to loopback only (binding all interfaces triggers a Windows firewall dialog).
